 Contrary to the claim, the International Criminal Court has previously confirmed the issuance of an arrest warrant against Senator Bato Dela Rosa 
 AT A GLANCE
 The International Criminal Court (ICC) has confirmed the existence of an arrest warrant against Senator Ronald 'Bato' dela Rosa, contrary to claims that it is fake.
 Dela Rosa is accused of crimes against humanity related to the drug war under former President Rodrigo Duterte and remains in hiding with a P50 million bounty on his head.
 Previous fact checks have debunked multiple false claims regarding the status of the arrest warrant and Dela Rosa's situation.
 This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors . 
 Claim: The International Criminal Court (ICC) said that the arrest warrant against Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa is fake. 
 Rating: FALSE 
 Why we fact-checked this: The Facebook reel bearing the claim has already received 1.3 million views, 10,000 shares, and 2,800 comments as of writing. It was posted on November 8 and continues to gain traction up to this date.
 The text overlaid on the video reads, “ ICC na nagsabi na hindi wanted si Bato bakit ang Pilipinas gusto [mahuli] si Bato may 50 million pa .”
 (The ICC has stated that Bato is not a wanted person. Why, then, does the Philippines want to capture him with a 50-million [peso] bounty?)
 The video also shows a photo of ICC Trial Chamber III Presiding Judge Joanna Korner holding a document labeled “confirmed fake.” Photos of Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla, National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag, and President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. are also featured in the video.
 More text overlaid on the video reads, “ Bulabog na! Shocking! ICC kumanta na! Hindi wanted si Bato! Yari kayo ngayon!” 
 (Chaotic! Shocking! The ICC has finally spoken! Bato isn’t a wanted man! You’re in big trouble now!)
 The facts: Contrary to the claim, the ICC has previously confirmed the issuance of an arrest warrant against Dela Rosa. The ICC has not made any official statement on its website or status conferences saying that the arrest warrant is fake, or that Dela Rosa was not being sought by law enforcement under an active warrant.
 The warrant remains active and can be accessed through the official ICC website. It was originally issued as secret in November 2025 and was only unsealed in May 2026. 
 Dela Rosa is alleged to have committed a crime against humanity of murder and of being among the perpetrators of the drug war under former president Rodrigo Duterte, who is currently detained in The Hague, Netherlands. 
 The international tribunal said that Dela Rosa, as Duterte’s police chief during his administration, knew about the operations and the scope of the war on drugs, created a network of perpetrators, controlled a structure of power, encouraged killings as part of the campaign, and threatened the ICC and fuelled disinformation about the drug war.
 In hiding: Dela Rosa is currently in hiding, with a P50 million bounty offered for his arrest. 
 He was last seen at the Senate in May, appearing after months of absence from the chamber in a surprise move to cast his vote in a leadership coup against former Senate president Tito Sotto. At the time, the ICC had already publicized the arrest warrant against him. Dela Rosa then reportedly escaped from the Senate premises on May 14. 
 Previous fact checks: Rappler has fact-checked posts falsely claiming an invalidated arrest warrant against Dela Rosa. In November alone, at least three false claims — including the Supreme Court’s supposed dismissal of the warrant, a fake quote card of Dela Rosa denying the existence of the warrant, and a misused old video of Remulla saying no such warrant exists — have been debunked. 
 Other false claims about Dela Rosa have also been fact-checked:
 FACT CHECK: No reports of Trump wanting to talk to Dela Rosa  
 FACT CHECK: ‘Shoot-to-kill’ Bato dela Rosa warning by Lordan Suan is fake  
 FACT CHECK: No basis for claim that Bato Dela Rosa is under Trump’s protection  
 FACT CHECK: Bato dela Rosa not yet arrested; online posts misuse old video  
 FACT CHECK: Bato dela Rosa not at recent INC rallies; post uses January 2025 video  
 – Angelee Kaye Abelinde/Rappler.com  
 Angelee Kaye Abelinde is a student journalist based in Naga City, and an alumna of Rappler’s Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship 2024.  
 Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.
